<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-almond" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-almond-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of almond, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

id="hmi-occurrence-almond-methods" data-shared-occurrence-methods><summary>Shared dataset methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:almond-db9eadc81078:de924734a21c"><summary>HMI almond Pb reference · Almond, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:almond-db9eadc81078:de924734a21c"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI almond Pb reference · Almond, as sold. Almond, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤4</td><td>≤18.5</td><td>≤52</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤4</td><td>≤20</td><td>≤53</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>53 reference units; 5 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>46</td><td>20%</td></tr><tr><td>FDA Total Diet Study</td><td>3</td><td>20%</td></tr><tr><td>Grembecka et al. 2013</td><td>1</td><td>20%</td></tr><tr><td>Marques et al. 2021</td><td>2</td><td>20%</td></tr><tr><td>Spungen et al. 2024</td><td>1</td><td>20%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for almond, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤50</td><td>≤50</td><td>≤50</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤50</td><td>≤50</td><td>≤50</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>2 reference units; 1 sampling family. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Marques et al. 2021</td><td>2</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for almond, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>Marques et al. 2021 is the only compatible sampling family for almond, as sold on this basis in the completed almond ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/marques2021-trace-elements-milks-plant-based-drinks" class="internal" data-slug="sources/marques2021-trace-elements-milks-plant-based-drinks" data-no-cite-meta>Marques et al. 2021</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:almond-7250e2ce19f0:f9d224fb8938</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Different HMI scopes are not one common ranking.</p></details></div></details><div hidden data-form-reasons><p data-reason="no_numeric_value_or_bound" data-title="Spread or extreme value only">The source reports only a percentile, range or maximum for these samples, with no mean or median to place against the reference. ## Processing, cooking and preparation

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-017"></a>

Processed or prepared forms were compared only with unprocessed almond in the same study and group. Almond, cooked (market samples, Konya Province, Turkey (2021 products)) had lead higher at 73 µg/kg, against 55.2 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (almond, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Akçay Kulluk D, Gökmen F, Dursun N, Özcan MM, Lemiashonak V · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals">Characterization of Heavy Metals in Some Edible Dried Fruits and Nuts Using Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectroscopy</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Erwerbs-Obstbau (Springer); accepted 26 November 2022; volume and pages not printed in the filed PDF</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Forms differ in water content, so a per-kilogram difference is not by itself a measured removal or gain of metal.

<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in almond?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same almond.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Akçay Kulluk D, Gökmen F, Dursun N, Özcan MM, Lemiashonak V · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals">Characterization of Heavy Metals in Some Edible Dried Fruits and Nuts Using Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectroscopy</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Erwerbs-Obstbau (Springer); accepted 26 November 2022; volume and pages not printed in the filed PDF</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Almond, cooked (market samples, Konya Province, Turkey (2021 products)) had lead higher at 73 µg/kg, against 55.2 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (almond, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Akçay Kulluk D, Gökmen F, Dursun N, Özcan MM, Lemiashonak V · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals">Characterization of Heavy Metals in Some Edible Dried Fruits and Nuts Using Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectroscopy</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Erwerbs-Obstbau (Springer); accepted 26 November 2022; volume and pages not printed in the filed PDF</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kulluk2023-konya-dried-fruits-nuts-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-almond-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-almond-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in almond is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in almond is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 4 results from 2 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) 2014 reported inorganic arsenic at 10.8 µg/kg (mean) in almond, as sold from European dietary-survey occurrence data.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
